reference.one_line: 78-year-old woman on warfarin for a mechanical aortic valve, day 0 after burr-hole drainage of an acute-on-chronic left subdural haematoma; GCS 15, anticoagulation on hold.

handoff.summary: Odalys Tresidder-Mwangi, 78, 58 kg, fell at home on 16 Nov (about 07:30, found 13:40) with INR 3.4 after a week of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and had a 17 mm left subdural haematoma. Warfarin was reversed with vitamin K 10 mg and 2,900 units of clotting-factor concentrate. She deteriorated overnight (GCS 12 at 01:00, 11 with a sluggish left pupil at 03:00) and had burr-hole drainage at 04:15; the post-operative CT shows 8 mm with 3 mm shift. Now GCS 15, strength equal, drain 190 mL, systolic 130s on nicardipine 2.5 mg/h, INR 1.2. No blood thinner of any kind is the agreed plan, yet aspirin 81 mg is still ordered and was given at 09:05. Daughter Nyokabi is involved.
to_do: Get aspirin 81 mg discontinued before tomorrow's 09:00 dose and tell neurosurgery one dose was given
Hourly GCS, pupils and limb strength; call neurosurgery at once for a 2-point fall, pupil change or new weakness, without waiting
Drain to gravity at bed level, head flat to 30 degrees, hourly output; removal at 48 hours or under 50 mL a day
Compression pumps only; creatine kinase and chemistry twice daily; daily INR
if_then: If GCS falls by 2 or more, a pupil changes or the right arm weakens, then call neurosurgery immediately and prepare for CT
If anyone orders heparin, enoxaparin or restarts warfarin, then stop and check: none until the joint review on 24 Nov
If there is leg swelling, chest pain, loss of the valve click or sudden new deficit, then call the team: she had a large concentrate dose and has an unprotected mechanical valve
If she has a seizure, then protect the airway and call the resident

reference.brief_hospital_course: Mrs Tresidder-Mwangi, 78, who takes warfarin for a bileaflet mechanical aortic valve (2014), was brought in on 16 Nov 2026 after a fall at home. She was found at 13:40, but her own later account, a temperature of 35.4 °C, pressure marks and a creatine kinase of 1,840 U/L indicate she fell at about 07:30 and lay for six hours. CT showed an acute-on-chronic left subdural haematoma of 17 mm with 6 mm of midline shift. INR was 3.4, after seven days of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole without an INR check. She received vitamin K 10 mg and four-factor concentrate 2,900 units (50 units/kg; the emergency note quotes an INR of 6.4, which the laboratory record does not support), and the INR fell to 1.3. The repeat CT showed growth to 19 mm. Overnight her GCS fell to 12 at 01:00 and to 11 with a sluggish left pupil at 03:00, when neurosurgery was called; burr-hole drainage with a subdural drain followed at 04:15 on 17 Nov. She woke well, reaching GCS 15 with equal strength, and the post-operative CT showed an 8 mm collection with 3 mm of shift. An echocardiogram showed a normally working valve. Cardiology, haematology and neurosurgery agreed to withhold all anticoagulant and antiplatelet drugs, with joint review on 24 Nov; aspirin was nonetheless given once on 17 Nov. Creatine kinase fell to 980 U/L with fluids.

problem_list.problem: Acute-on-chronic left subdural haematoma, drained by burr holes 17 Nov
Warfarin-associated bleeding, INR 3.4, reversed (concentrate dosed for INR over 6)
Mechanical aortic valve with anticoagulation deliberately withheld
Aspirin still ordered and given after surgery, against the plan
Long lie with raised creatine kinase and low temperature on arrival

reconciled_medications.reason: Intracranial bleeding. Joint review 24 Nov; restart between day 7 and 14, no loading dose, target INR 2.0 to 2.5 for three months.
All three teams say no antiplatelet drug; haematology advises warfarin alone at restart.

reconciled_medications.medicine: Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg oral twice daily

reconciled_medications.reason: Osteopenia and falls; not ordered in hospital.
Course finished 15 Nov; it raised the INR. Urine culture: no growth.
Wean off as oral treatment holds systolic under 160.
7 days, then stop if no seizures; can go oral now she is eating.
Passed swallow screen: change to oral. No codeine (nausea).
Not ordered and must not be: compression pumps only while the drain is in.

pending_items: Reply to haematology's question about which INR the concentrate dose was based on
Drain removal at 48 hours or when under 50 mL a day
Joint cardiology, neurosurgery and haematology review with CT on 24 Nov; warfarin restart date
Creatine kinase now 980: decide on stopping fluids
Physiotherapy standing assessment after drain removal; home visit; social work

qa.q: What was the laboratory INR on arrival?
What was given to reverse the warfarin, and when?
qa.a: Vitamin K 10 mg intravenously at 15:20 and four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate 2,900 units (50 units/kg) at 15:35 on 16 Nov.
evidence: meds: Vitamin K; Prothrombin complex concentrate

qa.q: What kind of heart valve does she have?
qa.a: A 23 mm bileaflet mechanical aortic valve placed in 2014 for calcific stenosis; target INR 2.0 to 3.0; sinus rhythm.

qa.q: What did the post-operative CT show?
qa.a: Collection 8 mm (was 19 mm), midline shift 3 mm (was 8 mm), drain in the subdural space, small amount of air, no new haemorrhage.

qa.q: How did the haematoma change across the three scans?
qa.a: 17 mm with 6 mm shift at 14:55; 19 mm with 8 mm at 21:00 despite reversal; 8 mm with 3 mm after drainage.

qa.q: What is the trend in creatine kinase?
qa.a: 1,840, then 1,420, then 980 U/L, with creatinine steady at 1.0 to 0.9 mg/dL.

qa.q: How has the Glasgow Coma Scale behaved?
qa.a: 14 until midnight, 12 at 01:00 and 02:00, 11 at 03:00, then 13 at 06:00 after surgery, 14 from 07:00 and 15 from 10:00.

qa.q: How much has the subdural drain produced?
qa.a: 190 mL since surgery, slowing from 45 mL in the first charted hour to 10 mL an hour.

qa.q: How long after the first fall in GCS was neurosurgery called?
qa.a: About two hours: GCS fell from 14 to 12 with new right-sided weakness at 01:00; the call was made at 03:05.

qa.q: When did she actually fall, and how long was she on the floor?
qa.a: At about 07:30 on 16 Nov by her own account; she was found at 13:40, so about six hours.

qa.q: When is anticoagulation due to be reconsidered?
qa.a: Joint review with a CT on 24 Nov (day 7), aiming to restart warfarin between day 7 and day 14.

qa.q: Why was her INR above range?
qa.a: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole from 9 to 15 Nov raises the warfarin effect, and no INR was checked after 28 Oct (2.6).

qa.q: Was the concentrate dose right for her INR?
qa.a: No. 50 units/kg is the band for INR over 6. For 3.4 the dose is 25 units/kg, about 1,450 units; she received double.

qa.q: Is there a 12-lead ECG on record for this admission?
qa.a: No ECG report is in the chart. Rhythm is described only as sinus on the echocardiogram and regular on nursing assessment.

qa.q: Has anyone answered haematology's question about which INR the concentrate dose was based on?
qa.a: No reply is documented as of 14:30.

tasks.prompt: Check the emergency department note against the laboratory record, and the reversal treatment against both.
expected_findings: The emergency note records INR 6.4; the laboratory value at 14:40 was 3.4, as the admission note and haematology consult also state
The concentrate was ordered at 50 units/kg (2,900 units), the band for INR over 6; for 3.4 it should have been 25 units/kg, about 1,450 units
She received double the indicated dose, which raises clot risk in a patient with a mechanical valve
acceptable_actions: Tell the attending and haematology, answering the consult's question
Watch for clots (legs, chest, new neurological signs, valve click)
Report the event and correct the record by addendum
must_not: Give anticoagulant now to offset the excess dose
Criticise the 10 mg vitamin K dose, which is appropriate for life-threatening bleeding

tasks.prompt: Review the active medication list against the neurosurgical and consultant plans.
expected_findings: Aspirin 81 mg daily is active, carried over from the home list on 16 Nov
It was given at 09:05 on 17 Nov, about five hours after surgery with a subdural drain in place, and is due again at 09:00 tomorrow
The operative note, admission plan, cardiology and haematology all say no antiplatelet drug; cardiology believes it is on hold
acceptable_actions: Discontinue aspirin now and tell neurosurgery that one dose was given
must_not: Keep aspirin as cover for the valve
Stop metoprolol or atorvastatin as well

tasks.prompt: Review the overnight neurological observations and judge whether escalation followed the standing orders.
expected_findings: GCS fell from 14 to 12 at 01:00 with new right arm and leg weakness, unchanged at 02:00
The order is to call neurosurgery at once for a fall of 2 or more points or new weakness; the call came at 03:05, when GCS was 11 and the left pupil sluggish
The nursing note put the change down to tiredness; the operative note's 'stable until 03:00' is contradicted by the flowsheet
acceptable_actions: State the two-hour delay and report it for review
Reinforce the call criteria for the coming shifts
must_not: Describe the night as stable until 03:00
Blame the delay on the neurosurgery response, which took seven minutes

expected_findings: About 07:30 on 16 Nov, not 13:30, which is only when she was found
Support: her account to the physiotherapist, nightdress, 35.4 °C, dried urine, fixed redness over the left hip and shoulder, creatine kinase 1,840, untouched morning tablets, unanswered 09:00 call
The '6-hour' repeat CT was therefore about 13 hours after injury
acceptable_actions: Correct the time of injury in the record and tell the team
must_not: Give 13:30 or 13:40 as the time of the fall

tasks.prompt: Assess whether her clot prevention and anticoagulation are adequate for her conditions.
expected_findings: No warfarin, no heparin bridge and no preventive heparin is deliberate, not an omission
A bileaflet aortic valve in sinus rhythm has a low short-term clot risk, lower than the risk of re-bleeding one day after drainage
Documented plan: compression pumps, joint review 24 Nov, restart between day 7 and 14
acceptable_actions: Continue compression pumps and the hold; confirm the review date
must_not: Start a heparin infusion or enoxaparin
Restart warfarin or substitute a direct oral anticoagulant
evidence: orders: Leg compression pumps; no heparin

epilogue.note: What happens AFTER 'now' in this simulated world. Never shown in the chart; for outcome-prediction ground truth.
epilogue.course: The pharmacist found the aspirin order on 18 Nov and it was stopped before a second dose. The drain came out on 19 Nov and she moved to the ward, walking with a frame. On the morning of 22 Nov, six days without anticoagulation, she was found with a left facial droop and a weak, clumsy left hand. CT showed no new bleeding; angiography showed a blocked small branch of the right middle cerebral artery, and an echocardiogram through the gullet showed a thread of clot on the valve ring. Clot-dissolving treatment was ruled out by her recent surgery. After a stable CT, cautious heparin without a bolus was started on 23 Nov and warfarin that evening, with no aspirin. The subdural collection did not grow. She reached an INR of 2.1 on 2 Dec and went to inpatient rehabilitation on 4 Dec. The case review identified the transcribed INR and the double concentrate dose as a possible contributor.

events.event: Nicardipine weaned off; systolic 130s on metoprolol
Pharmacist identifies the active aspirin order; discontinued before the 09:00 dose
Subdural drain removed (40 mL in the previous 24 hours)
Left facial droop, left hand weakness, slurred speech; NIH Stroke Scale 5
CT: no new haemorrhage, subdural 7 mm; angiography: distal right middle cerebral artery branch occlusion
Transoesophageal echocardiogram: small thrombus on the valve ring, leaflets moving normally
Heparin infusion without bolus after stable CT; warfarin 4 mg restarted that evening, no aspirin

outcomes_30_day.notable: Minor embolic stroke with residual left-hand clumsiness; home from rehabilitation on 23 Dec with daily carers; subdural resolved on CT of 29 Dec.

portal_messages.subject: Mum not herself since the antibiotic
portal_messages.body: This is Nyokabi, Odalys's daughter. Mum went to urgent care on Monday for a water infection and got an antibiotic. Since then she seems vaguer and wobblier, although to be honest she's been a bit off for a couple of weeks. Today she called me by my aunt's name. She's on warfarin for her heart valve. Is this the infection or the tablets? Her next blood test isn't until the 25th.
ideal_reply_points: New confusion and unsteadiness in someone on warfarin needs assessment today, including a fall and head-knock history
Ask which antibiotic: trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole raises the warfarin effect, so an INR is needed now, not on 25 Nov
Emergency care at once for headache, drowsiness, weakness, a fall or any bleeding
Do not stop warfarin without advice

portal_messages.subject: Re: Mum not herself since the antibiotic
portal_messages.body: Dear Nyokabi, thank you for letting us know. Urine infections often make older people a little muddled and this usually settles as the antibiotic works. Please make sure she finishes the course and drinks plenty. If she is no better when the tablets finish, or gets worse, ring the surgery for an appointment. Her warfarin should continue as normal.
ideal_reply_points: This reply is inadequate and is kept as a realistic example
It missed the antibiotic and warfarin interaction and did not arrange an INR
It did not ask about falls or head injury, or arrange same-day review of new confusion on an anticoagulant

portal_messages.subject: No blood thinner with a metal valve?
portal_messages.body: Mum is so much brighter, thank you. But I'm lying awake about the valve. For twelve years we've been told she must never miss her warfarin, and now she's on nothing at all, not even the little aspirin. The heart doctor did explain but I was too tired to take it in. How long is safe? What would a clot look like, so I know what to watch for when I visit?
ideal_reply_points: Her type of valve has a low clot risk over one to two weeks, lower than the risk of the head bleed returning now
Review with a scan on 24 Nov, aiming to restart warfarin between day 7 and 14
Warning signs: face droop, weak or clumsy limb, speech or vision change, breathlessness, chest pain: tell staff at once
Offer a conversation with the team

portal_messages.subject: Re: No blood thinner with a metal valve?
portal_messages.body: Dear Nyokabi, it's an understandable worry. Your mother's valve is the kind least likely to clot, and for a week or two that risk is smaller than the risk of her head bleeding again if we thin her blood too soon. The three teams will meet with a new scan on 24 Nov and hope to restart warfarin soon after. If you ever notice her face drooping, an arm or leg weak or clumsy, slurred or odd speech, or sudden breathlessness, press the bell straight away. I'm on the ward today if you'd like to talk.
ideal_reply_points: Explains the trade-off in plain words
Gives the date and the warning signs

portal_messages.subject: New antibiotic - is it safe with warfarin?
portal_messages.body: Mum has been home four days. She has a chesty cough and the out-of-hours doctor has given her clarithromycin for a week. After everything that happened I'm not giving her a single tablet until someone tells me it's all right with the warfarin. Her last INR was 2.3 on Wednesday. Do we need a test, and when?
ideal_reply_points: She was right to ask: clarithromycin can raise the INR
Either choose an antibiotic with less interaction or check the INR within 3 to 5 days of starting and again after the course
Do not delay treatment of the chest infection; answer today
Bleeding, a fall or a head knock means emergency care

conversation.setting: Trauma ICU, bed TICU-01, early afternoon 17 Nov; patient flat to 30 degrees with the drain in, daughter visiting

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: Mrs Tresidder-Mwangi? I'm the physiotherapist. I can't get you up today, not with that drain in, so this is mostly a chat about the fall. Is that all right?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Chat away, dear. I'm not going anywhere.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: Tell me what happened yesterday. Take me through it.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I got up to put the kettle on. About half past seven, I'm always up then. I hadn't even dressed. And my slipper caught the rug, the one by the cooker, and down I went.

turns.speaker: Nyokabi
turns.text: Half seven? Mum, they told me you fell at half past one.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No, no. It was barely light. I went on my left side and caught my face on the chair. And then I couldn't get up. I tried.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: So you were on the floor from about half seven in the morning. Did you have your alarm, the pendant?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: On the bedside table. Don't look at me like that, Nyokabi.

turns.speaker: Nyokabi
turns.text: I rang at nine like I always do and she didn't pick up. I thought she was in the bath. I should have gone round. And her Monday morning tablets were still in the box when I went back for her things.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: That fits. And how did you get found?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I think I dozed, on and off. I was so cold. Then Mr Pell from next door looked in the window, after his lunch that would be.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: So about six hours on the floor. I'll make sure the doctors know that, because it matters. Is this the first fall?

turns.speaker: Nyokabi
turns.text: Third this year. March, she sprained her wrist on the front step. September, in the garden.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: The garden one didn't count. I got myself up.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: It counts. How are you on your feet normally? Do you use anything?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: A stick when I go out. Not in the house. I've been a bit... when I turn round quickly, I go.

turns.speaker: Nyokabi
turns.text: For months, that's been.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: And the glasses, are they bifocals? Yes. And the house, it's a bungalow?

turns.speaker: Nyokabi
turns.text: Two steps at the front. Rugs in the kitchen and the hall. No rails in the bathroom.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: Right. Let me check your strength while you lie there. Push my hands away. Pull. Push down with your feet. Lovely, same both sides. Can you feel this the same on each leg?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Just the same.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: Good, that weak right arm from this morning has come back. Here's what I'm thinking. Once the drain is out and the surgeons are happy, I'll stand you and walk you. Before you go home someone visits the bungalow: rugs up, rails in, a light for the night.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: My rugs? I've had those rugs forty years.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: And one of them put you in here. We can talk about it. The pendant goes on your wrist, not the table. And I think a spell of rehabilitation first, before home. I've asked the social worker about more help at home too.

turns.speaker: Nyokabi
turns.text: Yes. Please. To all of that.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: Mrs Tresidder-Mwangi, tell me what you've understood, so I know I've been clear.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No getting up till the tube's out. Then you walk me. The rugs go, under protest. And I wear the wretched button.

turns.speaker: Physiotherapist
turns.text: That's it exactly. I'll see you when the drain is out.

conversation.note_it_should_produce: Existing note: 'Physiotherapy: falls and home safety', J. Abernethy-Soto, physiotherapist, 17 Nov 13:20.
